Hi! My name is Kai and I am a HS student (grade 9) interested in physics, space, and how NASA solves problems. 

I hope you consider joining my team so we can have fun and solve problems together :) I am mostly looking for someone who knows how to code (or someone who has a claude pro subscription).
summary:
Long space missions push the limits of humans. The exposure to space radiation, different gravity, isolation, and living in a closed environment all pose threats to the well-being of astronauts. These threats can cause eye problems, bone density reduction, heart problems, weakened immune system, and fatigue. During trips to the Moon or Mars, there may be 44-minute radio delay back to Earth. Astronauts cannot afford to wait for a doctor from Houston; they have to identify these changes by themselves.
AEGIS BIO is an offline health monitoring cockpit to help astronauts track their daily health stats, analyze the state of their body, and prevent small problems from turning into emergencies.
Developed as one lightweight HTML file which works completely offline without any dependencies, AEGIS BIO comes with built-in AI assistant and interactive 3D body scanner. Astronauts can quickly log their daily check-up, compare their vital stats to earth baselines, and receive step-by-step NASA treatment plans, like when to wear a lower-body pressure suit, change their exercise routine, or go to a radiation shelter.
details:
Overview: Why We Built AEGIS BIO

Long space missions are tough on the human body. Astronauts deal with space radiation, isolation, a closed cabin environment, and zero gravity. Over months in space, these hazards cause real health problems:

  • Fluid Shifts & Blurry Vision: On Earth, gravity pulls blood down toward our feet. In space, fluids float up into the chest, neck, and head. The main vein in the neck swells to nearly 7 times its normal size, and that extra fluid presses on the back of the eyes—blurring vision (a condition NASA calls SANS).
  • Bone Loss: Without gravity making the body carry its own weight, bones lose 1% to 1.5% of their strength every month.
  • Radiation & Stress: Solar storms can hit with little warning, while poor sleep and cabin isolation wear down the immune system and cause exhaustion.

When astronauts travel to the Moon or Mars, radio messages can take up to 44 minutes to reach Earth and come back. Astronauts can’t wait for a doctor on the ground; they have to spot these health changes in themselves and know how to act.

AEGIS BIO is an all-in-one health dashboard that runs 100% offline inside the spacecraft. It gathers an astronaut's daily health numbers, evaluates their risks using a built-in AI assistant, and gives clear instructions on how to stay healthy.

What It Does & How It Works

We built AEGIS BIO as a 7-page spacecraft cockpit that guides an astronaut through three simple steps: Gather, Evaluate, and Act.

1. GATHER: A 10-Second Daily Check-In (Pages 04 & 05)

Astronauts have packed schedules, so logging health data has to be fast.

  • Simple Daily Form: Astronauts enter 15 daily health readings across five everyday categories: Heart & Blood Flow, Eyes & Head Pressure, Radiation & Bones, Workout, and Sleep & Water.
  • One Click Shortcuts: If an astronaut feels normal, they can click "Fill Healthy Draft" or "Copy Yesterday" to fill out the form in seconds.
  • Mission Logbook: Keeps track of daily logging streaks and lets the crew save or load their medical records as a portable .json file. We also built in one click test buttons (Solar Storm, Eye Pressure Spike, and Normal Day) so anyone testing the app can see how it handles emergencies right away.

2. EVALUATE: Spotting Problems Early (Pages 01, 02, 03 & 06)

Instead of making astronauts guess what lab numbers mean, AEGIS BIO turns their data into clear visuals:

  • Overview & Built-In AI Assistant (Page 01): A lightweight AI model built right into the code checks 14 health markers and 5-day trends without needing the internet. It gives instant risk scores for eye pressure, neck vein swelling, radiation, and bone loss, and updates a top status bar (NORMAL, WARNING, or ALERT).
  • 100-Day Mission Calendar (Page 02): Comes pre-loaded with 100 days of realistic spaceflight data (Days 150 to 249). Days are color-coded green, yellow, or red so astronauts can easily spot long-term trends.
  • Vitals vs. Earth Normal (Page 03): Compares the astronaut's current body readings side-by-side against what is normal on Earth (1G), showing exact percentage changes.
  • 3D Body Scanner (Page 06): An interactive 3D wireframe body model that astronauts can click and spin 360 degrees. When a health reading crosses a safe limit, the matching body part (Eyes, Neck, Heart, Spine, or Bones) pulses yellow or red on the 3D model.

3. ACT: Clear Steps to Fix the Problem (Page 07)

Knowing something is wrong isn't enough, astronauts need to know what to do about it. AEGIS BIO gives immediate, plain-English action plans based on real NASA treatments:

  • For Swollen Neck Veins & Eye Pressure: Tells the astronaut to spend 45 minutes in the LBNP (Lower Body Negative Pressure suit) and wear thigh cuffs before bed to gently pull fluids back down into the legs, plus cut back on salty foods.
  • For Fast Bone Loss: Tells the astronaut to add weight to their squats and deadlifts on the ARED resistance workout machine and complete a full 2-hour daily workout with the CEVIS stationary bike.
  • For Radiation Spikes: If a solar storm hits, the screen flashes a red alert telling the crew to stop their workout and move immediately into the spacecraft’s radiation storm shelter.

Challenge Goals & Scientific Accuracy

✓ 100% Offline & Self-Contained: Works with zero internet connection—critical for deep space.
✓ Real NASA Radiation Standards: Uses the 600 mSv career limit and solar storm rules from NASA-STD-3001, plus real ISS daily radiation averages (0.5–0.9 mSv/day).
✓ Real Microgravity Medical Data: Uses published spaceflight numbers for neck vein swelling (9.8 mm² on Earth

70.3 mm² in space, JAMA 2019), optic nerve eye pressure (5.8 mm alert line), spine stretching (up to 5 cm), and bone loss (1–1.5% per month, NASA HRP).
✓ Accessible Cockpit Design: High-contrast dark theme (WCAG AA compliant), full keyboard arrow navigation, and reduced-motion support for tired eyes in a dark cabin.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • For Deep-Space Missions (Moon & Mars): Gives astronauts a reliable "doctor in a box" so they can catch silent health issues,like vision damage or bone thinning,weeks before they become mission-ending emergencies.
  • For Life on Earth: Because AEGIS BIO runs in any web browser from a single ~130 KB file without needing Wi-Fi or cloud servers, it can be used to monitor people in isolated places on Earth, like Antarctic weather stations, submarines, remote villages, and disaster zones where the internet is down.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

  • Languages: Pure HTML5, CSS3, and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6) packaged into a single, zero-dependency file (index.html).
  • Custom 3D Engine: Instead of using heavy external 3D libraries that take a long time to load, we wrote our own 3D human body generator from scratch using HTML5 Canvas math.
  • Offline AI Model: We built a compact, 2-layer neural network (LOCAL_AI_MODEL) directly into the JavaScript code so health predictions run in less than a millisecond on any computer.
  • Storage: Uses browser localStorage for automatic offline saving, plus .json file import and export.
